en: If you're nearsighted and you just stop wearing your glasses, will your eyes slowly train themselves back to sharp?
Take a guess.
I'm Max, and this is Max Wise.
Let's look inside the eye.
Think of your eye as a little camera.
The cornea and the lens focus the light, and the retina at the back catches the picture.
In the most common kind of nearsightedness, the eyeball has grown a bit too long.
Light from far away comes into focus before it reaches the retina, so faces and road signs turn blurry.
Taking your glasses off can't shrink that eyeball back.
If it feels like you're getting used to the blur, your brain is just getting better at guessing fuzzy shapes.
Glasses for nearsightedness spread the light out a little, so the focus lands right on the retina.
Eye doctors say wearing them does not make your eyes worse.
For adults, the main cost of skipping them is simple.
You just don't see well, and that really matters when you drive.
For kids, going without glasses, or wearing weaker lenses on purpose, is not a safe trick.
Studies found it doesn't slow nearsightedness down, and it might even speed it up.
And if one eye stays blurry while a child's vision is still developing, the brain can start ignoring that eye.
That's called lazy eye, and it's best caught early.
So no, skipping glasses won't train your eyes back.
Get regular eye checks, and wear the right glasses whenever you need clear vision.
Stay curious!
